newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/FORE CALLS IN DEMAND ON RUMORS.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/FORE CALLS IN DEMAND ON RUMORS.

text.p: Call options on shares of FORE Systems Inc drew heavy interest Tuesday as the stock climbed on heavy trading fueled by takeover speculation, options dealers said.
"There seems to be a lot of interest on the buy side," a market maker in the options at the Chicago Board Options Exchange said.
He said one firm firm bought 2,000 September 15 calls and 1,000 August 15 calls.
"We've had buyers of the September 17-1/2s and the September 20s," he added.
In afternoon activity, FORE was up 1-8/16 at 19-11/16 on turnover of more than 7.3 million shares.
The computer networking equipment maker said its policy was not to comment on takeover rumors.
"There seems to be a lot of speculation," the options market maker said, adding that volatility, which had climbed around 20 points in early August, was up another few points.
A trader at the Pacific Exchange said volatility in FORE Systems options declined after the early August spike but then rose sharply last Friday, when fresh takeover talk emerged.
The September 15 call was most active, with volume of about 2,070 contracts. The September 20 call traded 1,525, the August 17-1/2 call traded 1,275 and the August 15 call traded 1,230.
Few FORE Systems puts were active.
The options trade on all four options exchanges.
Telecommunications companies Lucent Technologies Inc and Northern Telecom Ltd were named as possible buyers, analysts said.
Lucent said it did not comment on such speculation and Northern Telecom was not available for comment.
The options trader at the PCX said call buying picked up last Friday on talk that a buyout deal would be announced over the weekend.
"Today it's been kind of choppy," the trader said. "There hasn't been anybody really screaming but there's been a big buyer of the September 20 calls."
The September 20 calls, which had open interest of 1,873 contracts, gained 5/8 to 2-1/8.
The market maker at the CBOE said some investors were asking for 20 and 25 strikes to be added to the August series even though the August options expire at the end of the week.
"Due to the inherent risk of the gamma from an option with four days to go that far out of the money, we elected not to list them and suggested they trade something in September," he said.
The September series has options up to the 22-1/2 strike.
Gamma is the rate of change of delta, which is the rate of change in the option premium relative to a change in the underlying stock.
